chung.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
chung.Description: This course equips students with comprehensive knowledge of electronic circuits, starting from the fundamentals of semiconductor materials and advancing to the design and analysis of amplifier, operational amplifier (Op-Amp), and signal conversion circuits. It covers essential topics including diodes, Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs), Field-Effect Transistors (FETs), analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog conversion, and the operation of timer circuits, with practical applications in circuit design. Through a combination of theoretical foundations and hands-on practice, students will develop skills to analyze circuit behavior, design efficient electronic systems, and utilize simulation software for modeling and testing. The course also emphasizes safety, professional ethics, and environmental considerations in electronic design.
chung.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time
- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose
- Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

taiLieu: Adel S. Sedra; Kenneth C. Smith
clo: Understand the properties and characteristics of semiconductor materials and diodes, and apply diodes in practical circuit designs.
Explain the operation of Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs) and design and analyze BJT amplifier circuits.
Describe the operation of Field-Effect Transistors (FETs) and analyze their biasing configurations.
Investigate the functionality of operational amplifiers (Op-Amps) and design practical Op-Amp circuits for various applications.
Utilize simulation software to model, simulate, and analyze electronic circuits effectively.
Demonstrate proficiency in constructing and testing electronic circuits, while applying safety practices and responsibility in laboratory settings.
Integrate professional ethics, social responsibility, and environmental considerations into the selection, design, and lifecycle management of electronic components.
